sentences.text:
The revision petitioner/Accused was convicted by the Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Bhadrachalam in C.C.No.387 of 2006, vide Judgment dated 07.09.2007, for the offence under Section 16(1)(a)(2) r/w.7 (u)(v) and 2(ia)(mb) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for a period of six months and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/-.

entities.text:
Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Bhadrachalam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the same, the accused preferred appeal before the I Additional Sessions Judge at Khammam, in Crl.A.No.136 of 2007, and the learned Sessions Judge vide Judgment dated 01.07.2009, while dismissing the appeal confirmed the conviction and sentence imposed by the trial Court.

entities.text: I Additional Sessions Judge at Khammam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the same, present revision is filed.

2. Heard learned counsel for the revision petitioner and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State.
3.
The revision petitioner who was running Kirana store was prosecuted by the Food Inspector on the ground that he was selling adulterated oil.
On 07.09.2001, PW1 who is the Food Inspector visited the general stores and found five packs of oil in the premises.
The said oil was packed by Rama Krishna Sai Traders of Chilakaluripeta.
The said oil was kept for sale and human consumption.
Accordingly, he purchased the oil from the shop and from one sealed cover he had cut open and taken samples.
The said sampling was done in the shop and thereafter it was sent for analysis.
It was found by the lab that the sample does not conform to Bellier's test (Turbidity temperature-Acetic Acid method) contains Palmolin oil.
For the said reason of the groundnut oil containing Palmolin oil, according to the Food Inspector, it was adulterated and accordingly complaint was filed.

4. Learned Trial Judge having taken cognizance of the offence under Section 16(1)(a)(ii), 7(i) and (v)
and 2(ia)(m)(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, conducted trial.
5. Prosecution examined PWs.1 to 3 and marked Exs.P1 to P27.
Considering the evidence, the trial Court found that the accused was selling adulterated oil, accordingly, convicted the revision petitioner/accused.
The said conviction was questioned in appeal before the Sessions Court.

The learned Sessions Judge found that the procedure adopted by the Food Inspector while sampling,
was in accordance with law and accordingly confirmed the conviction of the trial Court.
6. Learned Legal Aid Counsel appearing for the revision petitioner would submit that the process of sampling was incorrect.

In fact, under Rule-22 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955,
the food sold in package condition shall be sent for analysis in its condition without opening the D. Srinivasa Rao, Venkatapuram V And M, ... vs The State Of A.P., Hyderabad, And Anr. on 5 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130087019/
1 package and along with original label.
7.

entities.text: Venkatapuram V And M, ... vs The State Of A.P., Hyderabad, And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, since the said rules were violated, the sampling itself is incorrect.

Further,
even according to the complaint, the oil was packed and manufactured by Ramakrishna Sai Traders of Chilakaluripeta.
The said firm was also not prosecuted.
In view of the violation of Rule-22 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, while collecting samples, the prosecution suffers from infirmity.

8. Accordingly, the Criminal Revision Case is allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence recorded by the I additional Sessions Judge, Khammam, in Crl.A.No.136 of 2007 and the revision petitioner/accused is acquitted.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.
